predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Samarkand, Farghana and Tashkent, the governorships of Nuh, Ahmad and Yahya ibn Asad

predecessors.name: Saffarid dynasty
predecessors.text: Khorasan and Balkh, taken from Amr ibn al-Layth in 900

successors.name: Ghaznavid Empire
successors.text: Khorasan: the Samanid domains 'were split up between the Ghaznavids, who gained Khorasan'

successors.name: Kara-Khanid Khanate
successors.text: Transoxiana, where the Ilig occupied Bukhara definitively in 999

ledger.x: 819: the sons of Asad ibn Saman become governors.
819: the Asad governorships are held under Abbasid suzerainty.
821: the governorships answer to the Tahirid governor of Khorasan (bridged).
873: Tahirid overlordship over the Samanid governors lapses (bridged).
892: Isma'il moves the capital to Bukhara.
893: Isma'il takes Taraz from the Karluks.
Spring 900: Isma'il and Amr ibn al-Layth meet at Balkh.
900: Khorasan is Isma'il's.
900: the Balkh campaign ends with Amr in captivity.
900: Isma'il invades Tabaristan.
3 October 900: Muhammad ibn Zayd dies and the Samanids take Tabaristan.
October 900: the fighting for Tabaristan and Gurgan ends.
901: the Samanid army takes Ray.
By 911: Sistan under Samanid control.
December 913: the Zaydi Hasan al-Utrush defeats the Samanid army.
914: the Samanids, whose amir Ahmad was murdered in January 914, give up the fight for Tabaristan.
January 914: Tabaristan and Gurgan are lost to the Zaydis.
After 917: the Sajid Yusuf takes Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray.

c. 919: Ray reverts to a governor of the Samanids after Yusuf's defeat (bridging). The Yusuf page: 'In 919 the Sajid was defeated' and he was 'imprisoned for three years'; it does not say who held Ray, but in 924 Yusuf took it 'from its governor, who had rebelled against the Samanids', so a governor answering to the…
922: Sistan returns to a Saffarid emir.
922: the restored Saffarid emirate is a vassal of Bukhara.
924: Ray falls to Yusuf again.
928: the Samanid general Asfar takes Tabaristan and Ray.
930: Makan ibn Kaki seizes Tabaristan and Gurgan.

c. 930: Ray passes to Asfar ibn Shiruya, who had taken it for the Samanids in 928 (bridging). The Asfar page: he acted first 'apparently as a delegate of the Samanids, but thereafter as a sovereign ruler'; 'Asfar now expanded his domains over Ray, Qazvin and other parts of Jibal' and he ruled 'Tabaristan and northern…
931: Makan withdraws under Samanid pressure.

c. 932: the Ziyarid Mardavij conquers Tabaristan and, with it, Gurgan. Makan 'then returned to Tabaristan, where he was defeated by the Ziyarid ruler Mardavij, who managed to conquer the region' (Nasr II page, no year; the Makan page: 'Mardavij launched an attack that conquered Tabaristan', undated, after Makan won a…

c. 932: the Banu Ilyas settle in Kerman as nominal Samanid vassals (bridging). The Banu Ilyas page: after the failed 929 coup against Nasr, Abu 'Ali Muhammad b. Ilyas 'fled south, eventually arriving at Kerman in 932'; he 'acknowledged either the Samanids or the Buyids as his overlords but was effectively…
933: Mardavij cedes Gurgan and pays tribute.
933: the Ziyarids hold Ray for tribute.
935: Vushmgir conquers Gurgan from the Samanid side.
935: Nasr II re-establishes Samanid control in Gurgan and makes Vushmgir a vassal.
962: Alp Tigin conquers Ghazna from the Lawiks as a nominal Samanid vassal.
968: Adud al-Dawla conquers Kerman from the Banu Ilyas.
980: the Karakhanids seize Isfijab.
981: the Ziyarid vassals lose their last land.
990: the Kara-Khanid Hasan Bughra Khan attacks the Samanids.
992: Harun Bughra Khan occupies Bukhara.
992: the Kara-Khanids leave Bukhara.
998: Mahmud is confirmed in Balkh, Tirmidh and Herat.
999: the Ilig occupies Bukhara for good.
999: the contest for Bukhara ends with the Kara-Khanid occupation.
999: Khorasan goes to the Ghaznavids.
999: the Saffarid tribute to Bukhara ends with the state.
999: the Ghaznavid tie to Bukhara ends.
999: the formal allegiance to the caliph ends with the state.
999: the Samanid amirate ends.

wars.name: Samanid Civil War of 888
wars.outcome: Nasr I and his brother Isma'il fought over the distribution of tax money; Isma'il was victorious and took control of the state.

wars.name: Samanid conquest of Taraz
wars.outcome: Isma'il took Taraz, capital of the Karluk Turks; further campaigns in 903 'secured the Samanid boundaries'.

wars.name: Samanid–Saffarid war
wars.outcome: Samanid victory at Balkh in spring 900; Amr captured; Isma'il invested with Khorasan.

wars.name: Samanid conquest of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Muhammad ibn Zayd defeated and dead on 3 October 900; the Samanids took Tabaristan, Gurgan and, in 901, Ray.

wars.name: Samanid takeover of Saffarid Sistan
wars.outcome: Sistan under complete Samanid control by 911.

wars.name: Zaydi restoration in Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Samanid army defeated at Burdidah in December 913; Tabaristan and Gurgan lost in January 914.

wars.name: Sajid conquest of Ray
wars.outcome: Yusuf took Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray after 917, was defeated and imprisoned in 919, and took Ray again in 924 from a governor who had rebelled against the Samanids; he held it briefly (925).

wars.name: Samanid reconquest of Tabaristan and Makan's revolt
wars.outcome: Asfar took Tabaristan and Ray in 928 and ruled them as a sovereign until his death in about 931; Makan seized Tabaristan and Gurgan in 930 and left a year later; Mardavij then took Tabaristan.

wars.name: Samanid–Ziyarid war
wars.outcome: Mardavij conquered Tabaristan (about 932), ceded Gurgan and paid tribute for Ray in 933; after his murder in 935 Vushmgir took Gurgan and Nasr II re-established Samanid control there and made him a vassal (935).

wars.name: Alp-Tigin's conquest of Ghazna
wars.outcome: After the succession crisis of 961 Alp-Tigin, a Samanid slave commander and nominal vassal, fled to Ghazna and in 962 wrested it from Abu Bakr Lawik after a siege of four months; the Lawiks recaptured it around 965 and were uprooted by 977.

wars.name: Samanid-backed campaign against Khalaf of Sistan
wars.outcome: Khalaf was defeated in August 979 by a Samanid-backed army; no territorial change.

wars.name: Kara-Khanid and Ghaznavid conquest of the Samanid domains
wars.outcome: Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand and Bukhara attacked from 990; Bukhara occupied in 992 and abandoned on Hasan's death; Bukhara taken definitively in 999 and the domains split between the Ghaznavids (Khorasan) and the Karakhanids (Transoxiana) along the…

wars.name: Samanid civil war of 994-996 (Fa'iq and the Simjurids)
wars.outcome: Sabuktigin and Mahmud captured Khorasan from the rebel Fa'iq on 23 October 994 and won at Tus on 22 July 995 after Abu 'Ali and Fa'iq had beaten Mahmud at Nishapur in April 995; Mahmud retook Nishapur in 996 and reconsolidated power in Khurasan.

certainty.note: Governorships and steppe frontiers (Karluks, Oghuz, Kimek) are approximate; Sistan, Tabaristan, Gurgan and Ray changed status repeatedly and are drawn soft.
The 999 partition made the Oxus 'the boundary between the two rival empires'.
